Hyperventilation involves rapid breathing that expels more carbon dioxide from the lungs than normal.  
This reduces the partial pressure of CO₂ in the blood.  
Less CO₂ means less carbonic acid forms in the blood, which lowers the concentration of hydrogen ions, raising the blood pH (more alkaline).  
Thus, partial pressure of CO₂ decreases and hydrogen ion concentration decreases.
